messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: CANARY ALERT: deploy_2026_03_15_eu (eu-west) reporting sustained 5xx spike in green pool — paging oncall.
Maria Chen: oncall here, ack. observed spike aligns with the eu canary flip at ~11:23 UTC. how many users impacted?
Samir Patel: I pushed the canary to green pool (20% traffic target) via blue/green route update. deploy id deploy_2026_03_15_eu. no errors in staging.
Maria Chen: logs? sample 502s or 504s?
Samir Patel: mostly 502s from inference-runtime, some 503s from edge. short log tail below:
```
[11:24:12] runtime: request_id=abc123 status=502 path=/v1/generate latency=180ms pool=green instance=gw-eu-12
[11:24:13] runtime: request_id=def456 status=502 path=/v1/generate latency=210ms pool=green instance=gw-eu-07
[11:24:18] proxy: upstream reset by peer, eof
```
Maria Chen: OK. initial hypothesis: green pool instances are failing post-rollout. any config change that could cause this?
Samir Patel: only change was kernel selector bump and a small runtime env var for KV cache size (CACHE_MAX=1G). that should be safe.
Jamal Rivers: paging in from prod-sre. i'm joining. canary traffic fraction, confirmed 20% — but DNS telemetry shows some eu nodes still resolving old blue->green target incorrectly. TTLs seemed to overlap.
Morgan (Prod Eng): I see cross-region mismatch too — some edge POPs routed 100% to green due to stale DNS at the CDN layer (old records still pointing to green pool) while others stuck on blue. Mixed routing + failing green leads to partial outage symptoms.
Katie Lopez: Support: customers reporting intermittent failures across EU; top-10 list, Acme & ByteRide complaining. estimated affected requests ~7% of EU production during spike.
Maria Chen: mitigation plan options: 1) feature-flag kill-switch for canary (ff toggle eu-canary off) 2) revert rollout (redwoodctl rollout revert --id deploy_2026_03_15_eu) 3) scale down green pool to 0 / remove from LB. Thoughts?
Samir Patel: I'm going to flip feature flag first (least blast). doing: `ff toggle eu-canary --off`
Support Bot: Notified Acme & ByteRide with status update template, link to incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1879990200
Maria Chen: feature flag toggle confirmed by Console at 11:31 UTC. traffic should return to blue gradually — but due to DNS TTL, some edges may keep sending to green for another minute or two.
Jamal Rivers: seeing error rate falling in most POPs, but gw-eu-07 still shows 502s. I'm isolating instance and draining it from LB.
Samir Patel: draining gw-eu-07, and rolling a quick restart for gw-eu-12.
Morgan (Prod Eng): restart succeeded on gw-eu-12, gw-eu-07 removed. 5xxs decreased to baseline by 11:36 UTC.
Maria Chen: customer impact cleared? Support confirm no active degradation reports after 11:37 UTC?
Katie Lopez: support: Acme acknowledged received msg, no further errors reported. marking customer-impact resolved.
Maria Chen: handoff — i'm going offline in 15m. Jamal please take primary for now. leave this thread open for postmortem notes.
Jamal Rivers: taking over oncall. action items: 1) open RCA ticket 2) check DNS rollout process and TTL overlap 3) validate kernel selector + cache config interaction 4) add a canary kill-switch runbook entry. I'll create tasks.
Samir Patel: adding temporary guardrails: block auto-rollouts while DNS propagation > 30s and add health-check gating on green pool.
Maria Chen: thanks team. quick blameless note: suspected cause = TTL-related traffic skew causing green pool to absorb more requests than intended while a runtime config change caused instance-level failures under that traffic.
Incident Bot: Incident resolved :white_check_mark: at 11:38 UTC. severity: P2. RCA ticket created: INC-2026-045.
Jamal Rivers: I'll sync with infra on DNS cache TTL and CDN purge behavior tomorrow. tagging infra lead.
Samir Patel: will revert kernel selector bump in next patch and run canary in staging with load that mimics partial traffic.
Katie Lopez: Support to follow up with customers with post-incident summary.
Maria Chen: closing thread; please add any follow-ups to INC-2026-045. :thumbsup:
